agents.grant-desc: Grants are addressed by sha256(agentDid).slice(0,16), and the AUP DSL has no hash primitive, so this page cannot sign or revoke one. Use the operator CLI: it requires an explicit expiry and keeps high-risk capabilities behind a second confirmation.
agents.grant-forbidden: agent.admin is not grantable and cannot be granted: settle_payment, change_wallet and change_role never run from the agent surface (spec §130).
agents.grants-desc: Records under config/agent-grants/ (admin-only). A write tool only runs while its grant is unexpired.

agents.studio-registry: no cross-node Studio registry in this platform version (spec §71 is a POST-MVP transport)
agents.tools-closed-note: Closed tools never run from the agent surface: orders / settlements / sales name buyers (admin-only, privacy); settle_payment, change_wallet and change_role are default-closed.
agents.tools-desc: Every tool the agent surface declares, with the capability it needs and whether it can run today. Read tools are always on; write tools need a time-boxed grant; closed tools never run.
agents.tools-legend: Status: available = runs today; unavailable = declared but the platform cannot serve it (reason inline).
agents.tools-source: Source: node scripts/arcblog-agent.mjs tools — 19 tools (read 9 / write 4 / closed 6). Re-run the CLI to re-verify.
agents.tools-write: Write tools (4) — require a time-boxed grant
posts.drafts-note: Publish copies the draft into public posts/; the source draft record stays here. To move it instead, use the CLI — node scripts/arcblog-lifecycle.mjs publish deletes the source draft (move semantics).
media.index-note: Each row is one index record under /instance/app/arcblog/media: id, title, AFS path, MIME type, byte size, indexed time. The path is the direct answer to "where is it" — select the text to copy it, this console has no clipboard primitive. The record only carries the AFS path: no public URL is shown, because the index does not store one and none is invented here.
media.limits-admin: The media collection is admin-only (networkRead + replicated both gate it to admin), because a record exposes the upload path.
media.limits-copy: No clipboard primitive exists in this console: copy an address by selecting its text.
media.limits-grid: The list/grid switch from the spec is not implemented: afs-list layout=grid is locked to 6 auto-fill columns and a columns prop is ignored at runtime (docs/arc-contracts.md §25).
media.limits-join: A page cannot join collections. Reference data is computed by the CLI, which scans posts / drafts / pages / page-drafts / heroes for the asset's AFS path, so this page never claims whether one asset is referenced — ask the CLI per row, or use the unreferenced list below.
media.limits-url: Spec §15.4 also lists "copy the address (AFS path and public URL)"; only the AFS path exists in the record, so only it is rendered.
media.orphans-intro: Every index record whose AFS path is referenced nowhere (the CLI's own unreferenced list):
media.orphans-order: Always run refs --id <id> first: it shows where the asset is used before you clean anything up.
media.orphans-record-only: remove deletes the index record only — it never deletes the binary file.
media.orphans-refuse: remove is refused while the asset is still referenced (exit 1, code CONFLICT): resolve the references first, or pass --force to override.
media.refs-desc: Where is one asset used? The CLI answers per asset id.
media.refs-note: refs prints count plus each referring record (kind + slug + path) from posts / drafts / pages / page-drafts / heroes.
media.upload-desc: Pick or drop a file. afs-dropzone is the platform's only upload primitive and is declared without props on purpose: this platform exposes no prop metadata for it (arc dsl schema), so no prop is invented.

Even a successful upload would not create an index record: the binary lands in your own DID space and the index stays CLI-maintained. Index assets with:
general.basics-desc: Site-level values. They live in this blocklet's own config collection and are read by the RSS generator.
general.basics-error: Not saved — the write was refused and nothing changed. Check that a value is chosen (or filled in) and that the runtime allows the write; the console shows the platform error.
general.basics-guard: Each field offers only its own record’s allowed values, so this page cannot submit an out-of-options value, and a field must be chosen (or filled) explicitly before Save. The current values are shown under “Stored records” — that list is the source of truth. Two platform notes: on a brand-new tab the prefill can stay empty until the page is reloaded or reached by an in-page menu click (arc-contracts §21.11), and the readers fall back to the documented default if a record was written out-of-band — see `node scripts/arcblog-settings.mjs general show`.
general.desc: Instance-level General settings: site name, language, timezone and the three Instance switches. One home for every "where is that switch?" question.
general.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage this instance's General settings.
general.init-confirm-msg: Creates any missing record with its documented default. Existing records are left untouched (the platform refuses to overwrite an existing path in create mode).
general.init-desc: Create only the records that are missing, with their documented default; an existing record is never overwritten (create mode refuses an existing path). These are ordinary records: the CLI and this page can both update them afterwards — arc-contracts §29.2 (corrected in Round 10) says a browser write to an existing record is not refused in general; it depends on the origin of the record, the write mode and the daemon process. If a Save ever fails, probe before deleting anything: delete + recreate loses createdAt.
general.scope-desc: These are Instance-level values: they are stored at /instance/app/arcblog/config/{general,switches}/<field>.json and apply to the whole node. The impact of every switch is written next to it below.
general.sw-agent-consumer: Consumed by scripts/arcblog-agent.mjs: when off, `run` refuses every tool and `check` reports the switch as disabled (fail closed). Takes effect on the next CLI run.
general.sw-agent-impact: Impact: every Agent Access tool call on this node. It does not affect the read-only public web surface.
general.sw-comments-consumer: No consumer yet — ArcBlog has no comment feature at all, so this switch is recorded only. It is not a fake control: the page says so, and the record is readable by the CLI.
general.sw-comments-impact: Impact: none today. Planned to gate a comment surface if one is built (spec §15.9).
general.sw-rss-consumer: Consumed by scripts/arcblog-rss.mjs: when off, the generated feed keeps its channel but carries no <item>. Takes effect on the next feed generation.
general.sw-rss-impact: Impact: the public RSS feed (and therefore every subscriber). It does not remove published posts.
general.switches-desc: Instance-level master switches. Every switch states its impact and whether anything actually consumes it.
general.title: General
general.language-hint: Value of the RSS <language> element of the generated feed.
general.records-desc: What is actually stored under /instance/app/arcblog/config/general/. This list is the source of truth: if an edit above is refused, the value here does not change.
general.site-name-hint: Channel title of the generated RSS feed. It does not rename the blocklet or the console brand.
general.timezone-hint: IANA timezone used for the <pubDate>/<lastBuildDate> UTC offset of the generated feed.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics & maintenance
diagnostics.desc: Self-check results, storage and index, permissions, background work, logs, backup and first-line troubleshooting — readable without logging into the server. Every command here is copy-and-run; this page executes nothing.
diagnostics.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to see this instance's diagnostics.
diagnostics.honesty-desc: An AUP page cannot execute server-side code — provider mounts are not loaded on this platform (arc-contracts §26.1/§26.2). So this page only visualises the last recorded self-check and offers commands you copy and run yourself; every value comes from an AFS record or is a literal command string. If the self-check card below stays empty, no snapshot has been recorded yet (no snapshot = 尚未运行): run the record command first.
diagnostics.cmd-record: Run the self-check and record it
diagnostics.cmd-record-help: List the checks and the record shape
diagnostics.snapshot-desc: Source: /instance/app/arcblog/config/diagnostics/summary/last-run.json, written by the record command above and live-subscribed. Freshness: the recorded-at time below. The page never runs the check itself.
diagnostics.checks-desc: Source: one record per check under /instance/app/arcblog/config/diagnostics/checks/, live-subscribed. `severity` and `ok` are shown as text, so the state never depends on colour alone. The row count is whatever the last run recorded — this page hard-codes no number.
diagnostics.checks-hint: If this list is empty, no snapshot exists yet — run the record command above. Empty is not the same as “all checks passed”.
diagnostics.storage-desc: `arc space check` is read-only and answers through its EXIT CODE: 0 = every layout is files and the index is fresh; non-zero = something needs migrating or has drifted. The self-check above records that verdict as the `space-layout` check.
diagnostics.storage-warn: Do not pipe that command: its JSON report grows past 64KB and the CLI truncates piped output, so a captured fragment is not a report (arc-contracts §4.1a). Run it bare and read the exit code.
diagnostics.cmd-repair: Rebuild one folder's ledger from disk (`--index` is the default; `--no-index` fails closed)
diagnostics.cmd-list: List app spaces with file counts
diagnostics.perm-desc: This platform gives the app exactly two roles: guest and admin (`blocklet.yaml` replicated.readRole / minRole). There is no finer-grained read grant and no member tier (arc-contracts §13; SPEC-REVIEW-001 §B6), so a lock-down must be expressed by the directory prefix a record lives under. The authoritative matrix is scripts/arcblog-permissions.test.mjs, which runs inside the fast tier (`npm test`) — it is not a doctor check.
diagnostics.cmd-perm: Re-run the guest permission matrix alone
diagnostics.logs-desc: The daemon log is the only log surface. ArcBlog keeps no separate log file: the operational CLIs print JSON to stdout and the page data surfaces record their results in AFS instead. Commands verified against `arc service logs --help`.
diagnostics.backup-desc: The AFS records are the source of truth; dist/ is rebuildable from source with `arc blocklet build`, so backing up dist/ alone is not a backup. `arc space sync` makes `--to` converge toward `--from` and is additive by default — `--mirror` DELETES destination-only files. Both `--from` and `--to` are required, so preview with `--dry-run` first. Measured (REQ-028): a destination folder that was hand-edited fails closed (`index has diverged from disk`, exit 5) until you run `arc space repair --folder <dir>`, or pass `--full` to read both trees directly.
diagnostics.backup-key: Keep an OFFLINE copy, outside this repo: node.key (content signing key) and .env.local (chain configuration). They are not AFS records; losing them loses the node identity / chain credentials. Never commit them and never write them into AFS.
diagnostics.cmd-sync: Mirror the space into an offline directory (`--mirror` deletes destination-only files)
diagnostics.faq-desc: Symptom → command or criterion. Every row points at an existing authority (an arc-contracts section or a CLI); none of it is an automatic diagnosis.
diagnostics.faq-1: A save looked accepted but the record is unchanged
diagnostics.faq-1-v: The toast is not evidence — read the record back (arc-contracts §29.4): arc afs exec /blocklets/arcblog/.actions/read --args '{"path":"<afs path>"}' --json
diagnostics.faq-2-v: Conditional, not absolute: it depends on the record's origin, the write mode and the daemon process (arc-contracts §29.2). Probe before deleting anything — delete + recreate loses createdAt.
diagnostics.faq-3: A record disappeared from a filtered list
diagnostics.faq-3-v: `filter` / `serverFilters` push a query to the index, and editing a record leaves its index entry stale (arc-contracts §15) — re-check through the directory listing: arc afs exec /blocklets/arcblog/.actions/list --args '{"path":"<dir>"}' --json
diagnostics.faq-4: ?page=<id> silently lands on the public home
diagnostics.faq-4-v: That id is not a registered page. The authoritative page set is the sidebar model — verify with: node scripts/arcblog-console-nav.mjs --check
diagnostics.faq-5: A read is denied for a signed-in session
diagnostics.faq-5-v: The record's directory prefix decides: check replicated.readRole / minRole in blocklet.yaml (arc-contracts §13). There is no third role to grant.
diagnostics.faq-6-v: Audit first (read-only), then rebuild one folder's ledger: arc space check → arc space repair --folder <space-dir>. Dev-instance test residue: node scripts/arcblog-clean.mjs (dry-run by default).
diagnostics.faq-7: A publish never reached the public site
diagnostics.faq-7-v: Record a self-check and read space-layout / resources (node scripts/arcblog-doctor.mjs --record); for Hub state use node scripts/arcblog-network.mjs hub refresh.
diagnostics.intents-desc: Source: the records under /instance/app/arcblog/config/chain-intents/, live-subscribed. A console chain button only writes an intent; node scripts/arcblog-chain-worker.mjs run (or watch) signs it on the chain — the key stays on the node — and writes the outcome back.
diagnostics.intents-noheartbeat: No heartbeat record exists anywhere in this codebase, so this page shows no fake green light and no invented last-seen time. The newest updatedAt below is only an activity proxy. Empty means no chain intent has ever been recorded here — a normal state, not an error.
categories.add-note: A page write stores sort=0; adjust it afterwards with the CLI in the advanced section below. The CLI accepts only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (slugify).
categories.cmd-merge: Merge this category into another (migrates every referencing post)
categories.cmd-remove-migrate: Migrate the references, then remove it (never leaves a dangling category)
categories.gov-desc: Merge a category into another, or delete it while migrating its posts. In the row you want to change, type the target slug into that row's target field, then press its button: the button only queues the action — this node's worker performs the rewrite, so the browser never touches your posts.
categories.list-desc: One row per record under /instance/app/arcblog/categories/ (live-subscribed), showing the stored sort value. Reference counts are deliberately NOT displayed: a page-side count could only come from the query index, which goes stale after an edit (arc-contracts §15), so the advanced section gives you the usage command instead — it scans the records directly.
categories.list-empty-hint: An empty list means no category record exists yet — the publish validator then falls back to the built-in technology / design / life.
categories.sort-desc: `sort` is a real record field and the CLI lists by (sort, slug): technology 10 / design 20 / life 30. This page never edits it — change it with the CLI command in the advanced section. Ordering is CLI-only: this page exposes no other reordering interface.
hub.apply-desc: A Studio applies to a Hub by DID; the relation stays applied until the Hub approves it.
hub.did-shape: Hub DID must start with did: (did:key:z… or did:…). This is a text-shape note only — this page does not validate a DID against any chain.
hub.direction-legend: direction studio = this Studio applied to the Hub · direction hub = the Hub indexed this Studio on its own initiative (§70.2). Both directions live in one list: a per-direction filter would go through the AFS query index, and editing a record leaves that index entry stale, so the row would silently disappear (docs/arc-contracts.md §15).
hub.id-hash: The record id and file name are the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256(Hub DID) — this UI has no hashing primitive, so it cannot compose that path. Writing hub/registrations from the page would create a second record next to the CLI's own; apply and index with the commands above.
hub.retry-note: Retry is per Hub: report one Hub's sync result with its own row command. One Hub's failure never blocks another (§113) — this page has no batch or serial action.
hub.sync-hint: Sync view of this Studio as reported by the Hub (spec §112). — means the field has no value yet (never synced); nothing is invented in its place.
hub.write-failed: Write failed — verify the record with hub show (a success toast is not proof).
ledger.amount-note: Amounts are raw strings exactly as stored (no rounding, no unit conversion); the asset is a separate field.
ledger.append-only: The ledger is append-only: this page has zero write wiring — it declares no server action and no event handler, and it offers no edit or delete entry point. A new entry is only ever appended by settling or refunding an order (spec §91/§92).
ledger.cli-desc: Every command below exists in the CLI help; the page never invents one, and it never runs one for you.
ledger.cmd-order-show: Read the order behind a row
ledger.cmd-ledger-order-type: This order's entries of one type
ledger.desc: Settlements and the append-only ledger: the two records behind every split, with the exact CLI reading of each.
ledger.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view settlements and the ledger.
ledger.hash-note: transactionHash is shown exactly as stored. It is empty with the manual payment adapter and before settlement; empty is rendered as an em dash, never as a made-up hash (this page fabricates nothing).
ledger.withheld-note: hubShareWithheld true means the Hub DID had no verified attribution, so the Hub share folds into the creator (spec §30/§33). The raw boolean is shown on every row that carries the field — records written before the field existed show nothing, and the page never claims a split the records do not contain.
ledger.kind-note: Ledger entry ids are deterministic: <orderId>:<type> for shares and fees, <orderId>:refund:<origin> for reversals (spec §90/§91) — that is what makes a per-order read O(1).
ledger.legend-settlement-fields: Settlement fields: orderId, creatorAmount, hubAmount, protocolAmount, asset, amount, policyVersion, status, transactionHash, hubShareWithheld, createdAt (world/settlement.yaml).
ledger.legend-ledger-fields: Ledger fields: id, orderId, type, from, to, asset, amount, status, policyVersion, transactionHash, createdAt (world/ledger-entry.yaml). No field is omitted.
ledger.ledger-empty: The ledger only grows: a settled paid order appends creator_share / hub_share / protocol_fee entries, a refund appends refund reversals. See the commands above to read them.
ledger.ledger-note: The list below is whatever the AFS directory currently holds; it makes no claim about being complete. Use ledger list --all (totalCount) or --limit <n> to bound or widen it.
ledger.paging-desc: The list is paged on the page itself: 20 rows per page, Prev/Next, the current page and the total all read from the AFS listing — every page is reachable, so no row is hidden. The CLI stays the audit path: no flags = the newest 20 entries; --limit <n> = the newest n; --all = everything (the JSON output carries count, totalCount and truncated).
ledger.settlements-empty: No settlement yet: settle --order <id> writes one settlement plus its ledger entries (payment and settlement are separate phases, spec §89).
ledger.status-note: type and status are shown as the record's raw values (type: creator_share | hub_share | protocol_fee | refund; status: settled | reversed). The label is neutral on purpose — this platform cannot switch copy by record value (arc-contracts §28.8), so the raw value is the truth and the definition is written here once.
ledger.title: Settlements & ledger
orders.amount-note: amount and asset are shown exactly as stored; the asset is a separate field, never assumed.
orders.cli-desc: Read-only commands that exist in the CLI help. Creating, paying, refunding and settling are operator steps — this page runs none of them.
orders.cmd-pay: Record a payment (operator step, manual adapter)
orders.desc: Orders are the entry fact of the economy: who paid, for what, how much, which Hub and when. Every row is an AFS record read as-is.
orders.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view the economy and orders.
orders.kind-note: kind is the order's own value: purchase (paid content/product) or tip (never grants access, spec §36).
orders.orders-empty: No order yet — create one with: node scripts/arcblog-economy.mjs order create --id <id> --product-id <id>. Show them at any time with: node scripts/arcblog-economy.mjs order list
orders.policy-note: The split rule of Q4: this is economy/policies/active.json (what `policy show` reads).
orders.q-desc: The six questions are answered from the records this page can actually read. Q1-Q5 come from the order's own row; Q6 is deliberately a pointer, because world/order.yaml has no transactionHash — the hash lives on the settlement and the ledger entry, which the ledger page and the row commands read. This page does not join records, and a per-record deep link (?id=) is not a platform feature here (measured in Round 14: $params.id is not substituted on a ?page= URL), so the split details and the hash are always reached through the row commands.
orders.q-hub-note: An empty hubDid means the order has no Hub (无 Hub); it is shown as an em dash, never guessed.
orders.q-settled-note: An empty settledAt / settlementVersion means 未结算 (not settled yet) — settledAt is written only by `settle --order <id>`, and only for a paid order (spec §89).
orders.q6-value: Not a field of the order record — read settlement.transactionHash / the ledger entry (row command below). Never fabricated here.
orders.readonly-desc: The page only reads AFS records. It never claims that a payment, a refund, a settlement or an on-chain action happened: those are operator steps and the records are the only evidence (spec §89, L-R14-2).
orders.status-note: status is the record's raw value: pending | paid | failed | refunded (spec §42). The label beside it is neutral on purpose — this platform cannot switch copy by record value (arc-contracts §28.8), so the raw value is the truth and the definition is written here once.
orders.title: Orders
factory.advanced-note: Addresses and transaction hashes read from node/factories.json; the public key is bound into the on-chain NFT template, and no key material is mirrored here. Whether a value is chain truth is decided PER NODE, never from the file header — see the attribution card.
saved.add-note: A page write stores exactly the three fields below — a real record under the reader's own DID Space user scope, so a refresh reads it back from AFS rather than from a cache.
saved.desc: A private reading list. Every record lives in the signed-in reader's own user scope (/user/arcblog/bookmarks/<slug>.json), which the platform only materialises for that caller — no other visitor and no other signed-in DID resolves the same list.
saved.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to keep a private reading list.
saved.list-desc: One row per record under /user/arcblog/bookmarks/ in this session's own user scope. The path is caller-scoped, not a shared directory: the same URL resolves to a different list for a different DID, and a signed-out visitor has no /user view at all.
saved.list-empty: Nothing saved yet. An empty list means no record exists in this reader's user scope — the form below writes the first one.
saved.slug-hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, exactly as it appears in /posts/<slug>. The CLI enforces the same rule.
saved.title: Reading list
saved.where-note: Storage: /user/arcblog/bookmarks/<slug>.json (this caller's DID Space user scope, AFS path /blocklets/arcblog/users/<your-did>/arcblog/bookmarks/). ArcBlog declares no blocklet.yaml permission for it: the user scope is authorized by the session, not by a replicated collection — measured (arc-contracts.md).
saved.cmd-where: Show both storage paths for a DID
saved.gov-desc: This page lists and adds; it deliberately does not delete. Measured (REQ-028): an AUP page validates ALL of its inputs on ANY action submit, so one empty required field blocks every other action on the page — a page-side delete would be hostage to the add form below. Removal is therefore the CLI's job, exactly as on the other console pages.
diagnostics.user-desc: `/user` is a CALLER-SCOPED projection of this blocklet's user fragment, not a directory in the app tree: for the caller did:key:z… it is the same directory as /blocklets/arcblog/users/z…/arcblog/ (measured, REQ-028). It needs NO blocklet.yaml declaration — the session authorizes it. A signed-out visitor has no /user view at all (404 AFS_NOT_FOUND), and a different DID resolves the same path to its own, different directory. `arc afs` cannot address /user (no AUP session → `No module found for path`) — use the page, or address the fragment by DID.
diagnostics.cmd-user-path: Print the AFS path of an app DID Space fragment
diagnostics.cmd-user-list: File counts per role for this instance's app spaces
diagnostics.cmd-bookmarks: Reading-list CLI (records addressed by reader DID)
diagnostics.user-warn: AFS_DID_SPACE_SCOPE_SECRET is UNSET on this daemon, so DID Space scope directories are PLAINTEXT (de-identification OFF). It is a DAEMON environment variable: ArcBlog can only register it as a production prerequisite (the `de-identification` doctor check warns) — it cannot set it, and it must not turn on AFS_DID_SPACE_REQUIRE_DEID before the secret exists.
categories.adv-desc: These commands do the same work as the buttons above, plus what this page does not offer (sort, seed, usage counts). Kept for operators who prefer the shell.
categories.enqueue-failed: Could not queue the intent — nothing was written. Sign in as the blocklet owner and try again.
categories.merge-confirm-msg: Every post or draft referencing this category is rewritten to the target category, then the source record is removed, by this node's worker. Nothing is queued until you press OK.
categories.queued: Intent queued — the local worker applies it.
categories.queue-clear-msg: Removes the record from the queue. Posts it already rewrote are unaffected.
categories.queue-desc: The console cannot rewrite posts itself, so a button only queues an intent. The worker applies it with the same code path as the CLI merge — and writes the outcome (applied / rejected / noop + reason) back onto this record.
categories.queue-legend: pending = waiting for the worker · applied = posts rewritten, source record removed · noop = nothing to do (already done) · rejected = refused, no data changed
categories.remove-confirm-msg: Every post or draft referencing this category is migrated to the target category, then the category record itself is deleted — by this node's worker, so the category is never left dangling (spec §15.4).
categories.status-note: The status text is read verbatim from the record. This platform cannot pick a localized label per record (a dynamic $t() key renders literally), so the machine value is shown — docs/arc-contracts.md §28.8.
categories.target-hint: Every row has its own target field: type the slug of an existing category there (the list below shows every slug). An unknown or empty target is refused by the worker with a reason — nothing is changed.
categories.worker-note: Buttons only queue the action. The node's worker (node scripts/arcblog-category.mjs watch) performs it — the browser never rewrites a post. This platform cannot run server-side code from a button click.
factory.truth-title: Is it really on chain? (per node)
factory.truth-note: Each node records the adapter that produced its facts, in THREE states — mock (simulation, never chain truth) · ocap (real chain, verifiable) · unknown (nothing was ever recorded; then `simulated` is null and `simulationUnknown` is true, i.e. no false 'not simulated' claim — D37b). The header adapter describes config/nft-factories.json only (adapterScope), so it must never be used to decide whether a node is chain truth (BUG-043/046 · arc-contracts §32(9)).
media.adv-desc: The same actions as the buttons above, plus what this page does not offer (adding an index record by hand, forcing a delete). Kept for operators who prefer the shell — never the only path.
media.cmd-add: Index an uploaded asset (the console cannot: the file lands in your own DID space)
media.cmd-orphans: Re-scan the unreferenced list and refresh this page's delete-candidate list
media.cmd-refs: Show where one asset is used (read-only information)
media.cmd-remove-force: Force-remove a record that is still referenced — CLI only, never a button
media.cmd-queue: Print the intent queue (read-only; also repairs an old status word)
media.cmd-worker: Run the worker once / keep it running (this is what executes the buttons)
media.enqueue-failed: Could not queue the intent — nothing was written. Sign in as the blocklet owner and try again.
media.gov-desc: Each row of the upload index below carries its own 「移除该媒体」 button; the page-level 「清理孤儿」 card handles several records at once. A button only writes one intent record — this node's worker performs the actual delete, so the browser never touches your records.
media.orphans-candidates-note: The list above is the 「将删清单」: exactly the ids this node's last scan found unreferenced. It is refreshed by the local worker (node scripts/arcblog-media.mjs watch) and by node scripts/arcblog-media.mjs orphans. Edit the field to confirm a shorter list — the worker deletes ONLY the ids in it, and re-checks every one of them right before deleting.
media.orphans-confirm-label: Ids to delete (explicit confirmation, comma separated)
media.orphans-confirm-msg: Only the ids in the field are queued; each one is re-checked by this node's worker before its index record is deleted, and an asset that other content now references is skipped and kept. The binary files are never touched.
media.orphans-count: Unreferenced records in the last scan
media.queue-clear-msg: Removes the record from the queue. Records it already deleted stay deleted.
media.queue-desc: The console cannot delete records itself, so a button only queues an intent. The worker applies it with the same code path as the CLI remove, and writes the outcome (applied / rejected / noop + reason) back onto this record.
media.queue-legend: pending = waiting for the worker · applied = the engine really deleted the record(s) · noop = nothing to do (already done, or nothing matched) · rejected = refused with a reason, no data changed
media.queued: Intent queued — the local worker applies it.
media.remove-confirm-msg: The index record is deleted by this node's worker — never by this page — and the worker re-checks first: if any post, draft, page or hero still references the asset's path, the intent is refused, the reason is written on the record and NOTHING is deleted. The binary file is never deleted.
media.status-note: The status text is read verbatim from the record. This platform cannot pick a localized label per record (a dynamic $t() key renders literally), so the machine value is shown — docs/arc-contracts.md §28.8.
media.worker-note: Buttons only queue the action. The node's worker (node scripts/arcblog-media.mjs watch) performs it — the browser never deletes a record. This platform cannot run server-side code from a button click (docs/arc-contracts.md §26).
media.media-standing-note: The list above renders every record of this upload index. The index is CLI-maintained — add one with: node scripts/arcblog-media.mjs add --path <afs-path> --id <id>. An empty list only means no asset has been indexed on this node yet.
media.queue-standing-note: Every queued intent record appears in the list above, newest first: a row is written the moment a button is clicked, so an empty list simply means nothing has been queued on this node yet.
categories.queue-standing-note: Every queued intent record appears in the list above, newest first: a row is written the moment a button is clicked, so an empty list simply means nothing has been queued on this node yet.
factory.queue-standing-note: Every queued chain intent appears in the list above, oldest first: a row is written the moment a button is clicked, so an empty list simply means nothing has been queued on this node yet.
hub.actions-desc: A Hub relation is keyed by SHA-256(Hub DID), which this page cannot compute, so each button queues ONE intent record and the node's worker derives the id and writes the relation.
hub.elapsed-unit: ms, measured by the local worker
hub.enqueue-failed: Could not queue the intent — read the queue below (a toast is not proof).
hub.guard-note: The queue refuses a DID that is empty or not DID-shaped (did:<method>:<id> or the platform z… form), and refuses a duplicate unless you pick overwrite below. Both end as rejected with a reason and zero data change. This is a text-shape check only — nothing here resolves a DID against any chain.
hub.index-cost: Rebuilding the content index is a FULL scan of every published post and every existing index entry, and it runs on the local worker — not in this page. Measured on this instance in Round 20: about 19 s with 3 published posts and 43 drafts. That is a magnitude, not a promise; the worker writes the real elapsedMs onto the terminal record below.
hub.queue-clear-msg: Deletes this intent record only. It does not change the relation or the index.
hub.queue-desc: One record per click; the worker writes its outcome back onto the same record.
hub.queue-legend: pending = queued · applied = the data changed · rejected = refused, nothing changed · noop = nothing to do
hub.queue-standing-note: Every queued intent appears in the list above, oldest first — a row is written the moment a button is clicked, so an empty list only means nothing has been queued on this node yet.
hub.queued: Queued — the local worker executes it.
hub.worker-hint: Run the worker once / keep it running: node scripts/arcblog-network.mjs watch
hub.worker-note: The buttons only queue — this page executes nothing. The record lands in config/hub-intents and a local worker performs it; a success toast is not proof, read the queue below.
hub.confirm-add-msg: Queues ONE intent: the local worker indexes this Studio (relation indexed, direction hub). This page writes no relation itself.
hub.confirm-rebuild-msg: Queues ONE intent. The local worker then runs the FULL index scan — expect tens of seconds, and it may upsert or tombstone entries.
hub.confirm-register-msg: Queues ONE intent: the local worker applies to this Hub (relation applied until the Hub approves). This page writes no relation itself.
factory.render-timing: First-load note: on this platform the projection is bound AFTER the first render, so on a cold visit every field below can read the empty placeholder — that means "not bound yet / unavailable", never "the record is empty". Expand the advanced details or reload once to bind it (measured 2026-09-28: no channel recovers on its own).
operations.render-timing: First-load note: on this platform the health / discovery projections are bound AFTER the first render, so a cold visit can show the empty placeholder for every field below — read that as "not bound yet / unavailable", never as "the record is empty". Reload once to bind it (measured 2026-09-28).
